facts.statement: The genus Palaeeudyptes was described by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1859.
The type species of the genus Palaeeudyptes is Palaeeudyptes antarcticus.
The genus Eosphaeniscus, described by Wiman in 1905, is a synonym of Palaeeudyptes.
The smaller species of Palaeeudyptes were about the size of an emperor penguin.
facts.quote: They were probably larger than almost all living penguins, with the smaller species being about the size of an emperor penguin

facts.statement: The largest species, Palaeeudyptes klekowskii, was estimated to reach 2 meters in length and weigh up to 116 kilograms.
facts.quote: the largest species, Palaeeudyptes klekowskii, estimated to reach 2 m long (measuring tip of beak to tail) and weighed up to 116 kg

facts.statement: A humerus identified as Palaeeudyptes was recovered from middle to late Eocene beds near Puerto Natales, southernmost Chile.
facts.quote: an incomplete humerus identified as Palaeeudyptes was recovered in southernmost Chile, from middle to late Eocene beds of the Río Turbio Formation, near Puerto Natales

facts.statement: The genus Palaeeudyptes is the namesake for the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.
facts.quote: The genus is the namesake for the subfamily of primitive penguins, Palaeeudyptinae

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationship between the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae and modern penguins is unknown.
facts.quote: The exact nature of the relationship of the Palaeeudyptinae to modern penguins is unknown

facts.statement: Palaeeudyptes is an extinct genus of large penguins containing four valid species.
facts.quote: Palaeeudyptes es un género extinto de grandes pingüinos, que contienen a cuatro especies válidas

facts.statement: The largest species of Palaeeudyptes measured nearly 1.5 meters in height.
facts.quote: las mayores midiendo cerca de 1,5 metros de altura

facts.statement: The supposed genus Wimanornis, based on two humeri from Seymour Island, appears to be a more modern synonym of P. gunnari.
facts.quote: El supuesto género Wimanornis, basado en dos húmeros de la Isla Seymour, es aparentemente un sinónimo más moderno de P. gunnari

facts.statement: The osteological characteristics of Palaeeudyptes were somewhat less advanced than those of Archaeospheniscus and roughly comparable to the gigantic Anthropornis.
facts.quote: En conjunto, sus características osteológicas parecen haber sido algo menos avanzadas que las del levemente menor Archaeospheniscus y estando casi a la par del gigantesco Anthropornis

facts.statement: The genus Palaeeudyptes existed from the Lutetian to the Burdigalian stages, between 48.07 and 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Burdigalian (48.07 to 15.98 million years ago)
